title: Firestore: documents, collections and querying by index

videos.script: Spanner made you think about keys. Firestore makes you think about documents, and about the indexes that answer for them. {{documents}} A document is a small map of fields with a path, like customers, c-17, orders, o-10001. Orders live in a subcollection under their customer. {{paths}} Every query reads an index, and there is no scan to fall back on. For one field, Firestore builds the index itself. {{single}} For two fields, you declare a composite index. On Google Cloud a query without one is refused. {{composite}} The emulator does not refuse it. You will watch it answer a query that would fail in production, and then make it strict in Datastore mode. {{weaker}} Then two customers buy the last bananas at once, in a transaction, and only one of them gets them. And you will page through the orders with a cursor, not an offset. {{cursor}} Last, the bill. Firestore charges per document read, written and deleted, so you can price a screen before you build it. {{bill}}
